official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 1920-0017 -  Award  of Contract for Construction Services for The Various Security Improvements & Repair Project [Non-Bid Award) to Rook Electric, Oakland, CA,  as the selected contractor. for performance of work described in the Scope of Work in the Contract, i.e., repairs and or installation of security equipment, as described in attached invoices in the cumulative amount of $20,950.00, and authorizing the President and Secretary of the Board to sign the Agreement for same with said contractor for payment only on work which was performed from May 1, 2019 through May 17, 2019.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management

summary: The Board approves payment of $20,950 to Rook Electric of Oakland for repairs and installation of security equipment, as listed on attached invoices. The agreement covers payment only for work already performed from May 1 through May 17, 2019. The contract was not competitively bid.

title: Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost - Teach for America - Community Partnerships - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost between the District and Teach for America, New York, NY, for the latter to provide five weeks of teacher training including four weeks of teaching summer school covering the following content areas: elementary reading, elementary writing, elementary math, secondary ELA, secondary math, and secondary science, at Roosevelt Middle School, for the period of January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2021, at no cost to the District.
headline: Accepts Teach for America's free teacher training and summer school at Roosevelt Middle
summary: This no-cost memorandum of understanding (a partnership agreement) lets Teach for America provide five weeks of teacher training, including four weeks of teaching summer school, at Roosevelt Middle School. Subjects include elementary reading, writing and math, and secondary English, math and science. It runs January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2021 at no cost to the district.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost - Alexis Lavine-Moore - Community Partnerships - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost between the District and Alexis Lavine-Moore, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide a series of gardening classes where students will enjoy hands-on learning of biology and ecology, and will gain understanding of food sources and how to nurture, respect, and enjoy them, at Thornhill Elementary School, for the period of August 12, 2019 through August 12, 2022, at no cost to the District.

summary: This no-cost memorandum of understanding (a partnership agreement) has a local provider teach a series of gardening classes at Thornhill Elementary School. Students learn hands-on biology and ecology and where food comes from. It runs August 12, 2019 through August 12, 2022 at no cost to the district.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Rene Ernesto Quinonez - English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Rene Ernesto Quinonez, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide safety intervention and youth development services program for newcomer students, as described in the Scope of Work, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department, for the period of August 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $66,200.00.

It runs August 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020 and is capped at $66,200.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Educational Organization Contract Re Field Trips - Cazadero Performing Arts Camp - Various District Schools
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Educational Organization Contract Re Field Trips between the District and Cazadero Performing Arts Camp, Berkeley, CA, for the latter to provide participating music students from middle schools, with assistance from student high school mentors, its outdoor music education camps, entitled “Jump Start In Music” and “Summer Music Camp” occurring from September 15, 2019 through September 15, 2022, at no cost to the District.

title: Professional Services Contract - Adkinstrak Timing Associates - Oakland Athletic League (OAL)

title: Professional Services Contract - HERO - Parker Elementary School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and HERO, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide a variety of counseling/ mentoring services to target student population - Title I, Latino, African American and Second Language students - in the form of Social Skills Lessons, Leadership Program, Mentoring, Professional Development, and Organized Recess, as described in the Scope of Work, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, at Parker Elementary School, for the period of August 12, 2019 through May 28, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $30,000.00.

title: Subcontract - Spanish Speaking Unity Council - General Child Care and Development Programs - Early Childhood Education

outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost - Jenelle McBride dba Study Buddy - Community Partnerships - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost between the District and Jenelle McBride dba Study Buddy, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide after school study sessions for students that focus on various academic needs in math, reading and writing, with collaboration between provider, teachers and parents at Redwood Heights Elementary School, for the period of August 5, 2019 through August 5, 2022, at no cost to the District.

outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Teri Smith - Oakland International High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Teri Smith, Oakland, CA, for the latter to supervise counseling interns, attend COST meetings and partner meetings throughout the school year, at Oakland International High School, for the period of August 12, 2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $25,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $25,000 for a contractor to supervise counseling interns at Oakland International High
summary: An Oakland contractor supervises counseling interns and attends student support team and partner meetings at Oakland International High School. The contract runs August 12, 2019 through June 30, 2020 and is capped at $25,000. It began before Board approval.

title: Nonpublic, Nonsectarian School/Agency Services Master Contract(s) - 2019-2020 School Year - Special Education Program
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution Number 1920-0151 - New Master Agreements or Contracts and Individual Service Agreements with Non-Public, Nonsectarian School/Agency Services for students of Special Education Program for Fiscal Year 2019-2020 in a cumulative amount not to exceed $22,000,000.00.

summary: This resolution approves new master agreements and individual service agreements with nonpublic, nonsectarian schools and agencies that serve students in the special education program. The total for all of them is capped at $22,000,000 for the 2019-20 fiscal year. The text does not name the individual schools or agencies.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Subaward Agreement - Strategic Education Research Partnership (SERP) Institute - (Extension of Time) - Academics and Instructional Innovation Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, SubAward Agreement between the District and Strategic Education Research Partnership Institute (SERP), Washington, DC, for the latter to support development of a year-long high school chemistry curriculum, as described herein, and accepting associated $80,000.00 grant award therefor, from the Koshland Foundation, pursuant to terms and conditions thereof, extending the term of the SubAward Agreement from October 1, 2018 through July 31, 2019 to July 31, 2020.  All other terms and conditions of the SubAward Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Extends SERP's chemistry curriculum work to July 2020; memo cites $80,000 in Koshland grant funding
summary: This amendment extends the agreement with the Strategic Education Research Partnership Institute (SERP), which is helping develop a year-long high school chemistry curriculum, from July 31, 2019 to July 31, 2020. The amendment document itself changes only the term. The district memo cites $80,000 in Koshland Foundation grant funding for the part-time science specialist, and the grant award letter lists $80,000 for the 2019-20 school year, so this appears to be the next year's installment rather than a restatement, though the documents do not say so outright.
source_issue: The official text accepts an $80,000 grant award in an item titled as an extension of time, without saying whether it is new money or the original grant restated; the signed amendment itself changes only the term.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - First Alarm Security & Patrol - Police Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and First Alarm Security & Patrol, San Jose, CA, for the latter to respond to Alarms and monitoring of sites when District Police Services Officers are off duty including District Holidays and weekends, as specified in Agreement, via Police Services Department, for the period of July 22, 2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $165,000.00.
headline: Pays First Alarm Security & Patrol up to $165,000 for alarm response and off-hours site monitoring
summary: First Alarm Security & Patrol of San Jose responds to alarms and monitors district sites when District Police Services officers are off duty, including holidays and weekends. The contract runs July 22, 2019 through June 30, 2020 and is capped at $165,000.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Side Letter Agreement - District and Oakland Education Association (“OEA”) - National Education Association (''NEA'") Community Schools Grant - Release Time
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Side Letter of Agreement, as Agreement between the District and the Oakland Education Association (“OEA”), regarding  the  National  Education  Association  (''NEA'") Community  Schools Grant and release time for OEA leadership participation, in particular providing for the release of teacher, Kampala Taiz-Rancifer, for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, pursuant to terms and conditions thereof, with the Agreement (Side Letter) in effect between the Parties from July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022.
headline: Approves a side agreement with the teachers union on release time for a National Education Association grant
summary: The district and the Oakland Education Association (OEA), the teachers union, sign a side letter about the National Education Association (NEA) Community Schools Grant. It gives a teacher release time from the classroom to take part in OEA leadership, for July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020. The side letter itself stays in effect through June 30, 2022. The text states no dollar amount.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Board on Track - Charter Schools Office
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Board on Track, Concord, MA, for the latter to assist the Office of Charter Schools (OCS) with appointments to charter boards as required by Board Resolution 1718-0168; develop video training modules to be used to train appointees to charter boards on the requirements and best practices of their position; provide OCS with thought partnership and support to OCS staff on designing reporting materials and matching applicants to charter boards; and in June 2020, provide selected boards with a skill appraisal to help OCS evaluate the skill set of board, via the Office of Charter Schools, for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $45,000.00.

summary: Board on Track of Concord, Massachusetts helps the Office of Charter Schools with appointments to charter school boards. It builds video training modules for appointees, advises staff on reporting materials and applicant matching, and gives selected boards a skills appraisal in June 2020. The contract runs July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020 and is capped at $45,000. It began before Board approval.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Redesignation of Recognition Date - District's 2019-2020 Teacher(s) of the Year - Board of Education
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 1819-0093A - Redesignation of Date of Recognition of Oakland Unified School District’s 2019-2020 Teacher of the Year.
headline: Changes the date for recognizing the district's 2019-2020 Teacher of the Year

The cost is capped at $2,000 and the contract runs September 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020. The Risk Management Department manages it.

title: Amendment No. 2, Contract for Services (Architectural Services Agreement) - DSK Architects – Frick Middle School Modernization Intensive Support Site Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management

Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 2, Contract for Services (Architectural Services Agreement) between the District and DSK Architects, San Francisco, CA, reimbursing latter for Fees paid on behalf of District to CA Department of General Services, as follows:

·	$5,000.00 "For core operating support of Skyline High School's girls varsity basketball team to promote physical activity";
·	$5,000.00 "For core operating support of Oakland Technical High School's girls varsity basketball team to promote health through physical activity"; and

Approval by the Board of Education of an Agreement for Inspector of Record (“IOR”) Services for Construction to Anthonio, Inc.*, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide Inspector of Record Services during construction including daily reports, punch list and Division of the State Architect (DSA)  close-out reports needed for the Sankofa Elementary School Portable Classroom Project, in the amount of $18,800.00, which includes a contingency fee of $5,000.00, as the selected IOR, and authorizing the President and Secretary of the Board to sign the Agreement for same with said IOR with work scheduled to commence on March 26, 2020, and scheduled to last until December 31, 2021 pursuant to the Contract.  
___
The IOR was selected through an RFP process. Competitive bidding was not required because price cost is less than $95,200.00 and the Agreement is for specially trained services.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Approves $18,800 for Anthonio, Inc. to inspect construction of portable classrooms at Sankofa Elementary
summary: Anthonio, Inc. will serve as the Inspector of Record, who oversees construction and prepares daily reports, a punch list and close-out reports for the Division of the State Architect, for the Sankofa Elementary portable classroom project. The $18,800 includes a $5,000 contingency. Work runs from March 26, 2020 to December 31, 2021. The inspector was chosen through a request for proposals, and public bidding was not required because the price is under $95,200 and the work is specially trained services.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

headline: Adds $18,432 to Bay Area Community Resources' after-school program at Global Family Elementary

title: COVID Amendment – NonPublic, Nonsectarian School/Agency Services Master Contract – Resolution No. 1920-0151 – Named Contractor - Special Education Department
official_text:
Adoption by the Board of Education of COVID Amendment by and between District and
§	La Cheim School, Inc., El Sobrante, CA; and
§	Star Academy, San Rafael, CA
amending Non-Public School/Agency Master Contract Resolution No. 1920-0151, (Legislative File Id No. 19-1716, Enactment No 19-1376, adopted September 11, 2019), in part, pertaining only to the Contract with named vendor, necessary in light of the COVID-19 Pandemic and the shelter-in-place order issued by the Alameda County Public Health Officer, and/or other authorities within and without California, modifying, among other provisions, the Scope of Work, enabling the vendor to provide the services described in the original Contract - Scope of Work - by any means that are consistent with COVID-19-related local, state, and federal orders (including providing the services virtually), as long as the District agrees in writing and adding a requirement for more information to be provided in an Invoice, and authoring no additional costs for said services. All other terms and conditions of the Contract remain in full force and effect.
headline: Lets two nonpublic special education schools serve students virtually during COVID-19 at no added cost
summary: This amends the district's existing contracts with La Cheim School, Inc. and Star Academy, which are nonpublic schools or agencies that serve some special education students. During the COVID-19 shelter-in-place orders, the schools may deliver the contracted services by any means allowed under health orders, including virtually, if the district agrees in writing. Invoices must include more information, and there is no additional cost.
vendor_name: La Cheim School, Inc.; Star Academy
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Performance Fact - Network 4
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 between the District and Performance Fact, Oakland, CA, after four years of design, development, implementation, and continuous improvement of a number of promising practices at the Lockwood Elementary School Campus, through the School Improvement Grant, at the Network level, and at the LEA (Oakland USD) level, for the latter to provide three strands: 

Strand #1: Assess SIG’s Impact
Assess and document “what we did, what difference it made, what we
learned” during the years of SIG implementation at the Lockwood Campus,
Network, and LEA levels, including compilation and analysis of evidence such as:
artifacts, video/photos, interviews and surveys, student outcome data, impact
on/of teaching, learning, leadership, and operations;
.
Strand #2: Design for Post-SIG Sustainability
Codify core tools and processes, including full documentation in digital formats
(e.g., Google Suite) that ensure easy access and wide dissemination, and
facilitators who would possess the knowledge and skills to serve as trainers for
others regarding the core tools and processes; and 

Strand #3: Focus Implementation in COVID-19 Era
Provide technical assistance regarding implementation of the specific 2020-
2021 annual priorities (i.e., work plan) at the Lockwood Campus, the Network,
and the LEA, with adjustments for the COVID-19 environment,

via Network 4,  for the period of December 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021, in an amount not to exceed $195,000.00.

summary: Performance Fact of Oakland will review what the district learned from four years of School Improvement Grant work at the Lockwood Elementary campus, the Network 4 group of schools and the district level. The agreement runs December 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021, and the work began before this vote.

official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Memorandum of Understanding between the District and Bay Area Community Resources, San Rafael, CA, adding to the Scope of Work set forth in the August 26, 2020 Agreement (Legislative File No. 20-1178, Enactment No. 20-1206) the following paragraphs to the existing Scope of Work: 

Amended Scope of Work

VENDOR will provide in-person learning supports to students in K-5 at Sankofa United Elementary School. In-person learning supports may include (but are not limited to) support with accessing technology, facilitating access to classroom zoom sessions, motivating students to complete work, providing one-to-one mentoring or encouragement, and connecting with supplemental services if needed, and other supports as directed by OUSD.

As set forth in Paragraph 4 of this Amendment, VENDOR agrees to perform these services in accordance with any shelter-in-place (or similar) orders (“SIP orders”), and to immediately follow all OUSD directives regarding health and safety protocols. Specifically, VENDOR shall deliver services in cohorts with student: staff ratios that comply with SIP orders and OUSD directives. In addition, VENDOR shall ensure that all staff participate in wellness checks (including proof of negative COVID-19 test results) in accordance with OUSD policies and directives 

All other terms and condition of the Memorandum of Understanding remain in full force and effect.

title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Earth Team - Skyline High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 between the District and Earth Team, Richmond, CA, for the latter to provide its Sustainable Youth Internships Program, operating in public high schools as an afterschool program, to help building capacity for engagement of diverse student populations in the environmental sciences at Skyline High School, for the period of July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021, in an amount not to exceed $5,600.00.

summary: The board is ratifying (approving after the fact) a 2020-21 agreement with Earth Team to run its Sustainable Youth Internships Program as an afterschool program at Skyline High School. The agreement covers July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021, and the district may pay up to $5,600, funded by the Green California Partnership Academy.

The work runs March 29, 2021 through June 30, 2021, for up to $3,000, through the High School Linked Learning Department.

official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) by and between the District Street Academy Foundation of Oakland and the District, for District to operate the Emiliano Zapata Street Academy, a 9-12 grades school of approximately 120 students, funded by pupil ADA and other eligible resources, if any, named in MOU, for the period July 1, 2021, through June 30, 2024, pursuant to terms and conditions stated therein.

The school is funded by student attendance funding and other eligible resources named in the agreement. The text states no dollar amount; the term is July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2024.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Data Sharing Agreement - University of California, Berkeley - Research, Assessment and Data (RAD) Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Data Sharing Agreement between the District and the University of California, Berkeley, CA, authorizing OUSD to share data with the latter, which will allow Recipients to use student-level data to characterize the influence of publicly supported preschool programming (Head Start and OUSD preschool) on children’s early learning and developmental trajectories through TK and kindergarten and examine the predictive power of common instruments of early development and learning (e.g. DRDP) with respect to kindergarten-entry measures of the same (e.g. EDI), for the period of April 20, 2021 through April 19, 2023, at no cost to the District.
headline: Lets UC Berkeley use student data to study how public preschool shapes early learning, at no cost
summary: The board is approving a data sharing agreement that lets the district share student-level data with the University of California, Berkeley. Researchers will study how publicly supported preschool programs (Head Start and OUSD preschool) affect children's early learning and development through transitional kindergarten and kindergarten. The agreement runs April 20, 2021 through April 19, 2023 at no cost to the district.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Myrtha Muse - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 between the District and Myrtha Muse, Oakland, Ca, for the latter to teach varied styles of dance with emphasis on Katherine Dunham techniques - prepare students for short performances at assemblies, prepare students for professional culminating performance for parents and the community at-large, introduce dance history; teach student West African Dance forms and rhythms from several West African nations; take students to Sharing Assembly of professional artists; have students perform at culminating program; learn basic fundamentals of drama and dance, experience integration of the arts and its relationship to math, via Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period of June 7, 2021 through July 2, 2021, in an amount not to exceed $5,200.00.
headline: Pays a dance instructor up to $5,200 for a June 2021 arts program with West African dance
summary: The board is ratifying (approving after the fact) a 2020-21 agreement with an individual contractor to teach varied dance styles, including Katherine Dunham techniques and West African dance forms, and to prepare students for performances. The work runs June 7, 2021 through July 2, 2021, through the Community Schools and Student Services Department. The district may pay up to $5,200, funded by Measure G, a parcel tax.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Corissa Johnson - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 between the District and Corissa Johnson, Hayward, CA, for the latter to plan and organize visual arts and/or instrumental music activities that are aligned to the CA Core Content Standards for Visual and Performing Arts; explore various art and music forms and show their relationship to ELA and Math; delegate responsibilities to build leadership skills; utilize visual and performing arts as a means of career exploration, via Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period of June 7, 2021 through July 2, 2021, in an amount not to exceed $5,200.00.
headline: Pays a visual arts and music instructor up to $5,200 for a June 2021 student program
summary: The board is ratifying (approving after the fact) a 2020-21 agreement with an individual contractor to plan and organize visual arts and instrumental music activities aligned to state standards. Activities connect the arts to English and math and to career exploration. The work runs June 7, 2021 through July 2, 2021, through the Community Schools and Student Services Department, for up to $5,200, funded by Measure G, a parcel tax.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Professional Services Agreement - Oakland Public Education Fund - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Professional Services Agreement between the District and Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland, CA, for the latter to process $8350 of additional direct payments to hotel/motel for McKinney-Vento Families moved from car to hotel/motel for respite housing and support the stabilization of distance learning for students, increasing the Agreement from a not to exceed amount of $4,850.00 to $13,150.00 and extending the Agreement term from August 10, 2020 through September 30, 2020 to June 30, 2021. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Adds $8,350 for Oakland Public Education Fund to pay hotels for families facing homelessness
summary: This amendment adds money and time to an agreement with the Oakland Public Education Fund, which processes direct payments to hotels and motels for McKinney-Vento (homeless) families moved from cars to temporary housing, to help stabilize distance learning. The text raises the not-to-exceed amount from $4,850 to $13,150 and extends the end date from September 30, 2020 to June 30, 2021. The stated increase and totals do not match exactly.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - PranaMind LLC - Sankofa Elementary School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 between the District and PranaMind, LLC, Oakland, CA, for the latter to serve as the lead consultant and to manage the continuing education process for approximately 25-30 educators and ensure delivery of two professional development training sessions; provide technical assistance in the form of a follow-up meeting either virtually or face to face (TBD); and develop a brain-based reading program for use by students at Sankofa United Elementary School, for the period of May 1, 2021 through October 31, 2021, in an amount not to exceed $6,000.00.
headline: Pays PranaMind up to $6,000 for teacher training and a reading program at Sankofa Elementary
summary: PranaMind, LLC will lead training for about 25-30 educators (two training sessions plus a follow-up meeting) and develop a brain-based reading program for students at Sankofa United Elementary School. The agreement runs May 1 to October 31, 2021, for no more than $6,000. The board is approving it after the May 1 start date.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Agreement UCAN – No Cost - Regents UC, on behalf of its UC Agriculture and Natural Resources and its UC Cooperative Extension – Alameda County - Community Partnerships - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Professional Services Agreement UCAN - No Cost between the District and The Regents of the University of California, on behalf of its UC Agriculture and Natural Resources and its UC Cooperative Extension - Alameda County, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide in District its Cal Fresh Healthy Living: See site directory, attached as Exhibit “B”: Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program at Lincoln Elementary; adult program varies year to year, target is low income adults with children in home; and Master Gardener Program: See MGP site list, attached as Exhibit “C”,  for the period of June 1, 2021 through May 31, 2024, at no cost to the District.
headline: Approves a no-cost UC Cooperative Extension nutrition and gardening partnership through 2024
summary: The University of California's agriculture and natural resources extension office in Alameda County will provide a food and nutrition education program at Lincoln Elementary, aimed at low-income adults with children at home, and a Master Gardener program at listed sites. The agreement runs June 1, 2021 through May 31, 2024 and costs the district nothing.
vendor_name: The Regents of the University of California (UC Cooperative Extension, Alameda County)
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 – No Cost - The Oakland REACH - Community Partnerships - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - No Cost, between the District and The Oakland REACH, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide literacy tutoring/support during the school day and after school, after-school enrichment opportunities via REACH’s Opportunity Fund, family partnership and support via weekly virtual family workshops and Equity Family Leaders, and virtual technology support and training for families, for the period of the latest of the dates on which each of the PARTIES signed this Agreement through June 30, 2022, at no cost to the District.
headline: Approves a no-cost partnership with The Oakland REACH for tutoring and family support
summary: The Oakland REACH will provide literacy tutoring during and after the school day, after-school enrichment, weekly virtual family workshops, and technology help for families. The agreement runs from the date both sides sign it through June 30, 2022 and costs the district nothing.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Grant Application - California Department of Natural Resources - Youth Community Access Program Grant - English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement (ELLMA) Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of District Grant Application to the California Department of Natural Resources seeking Youth Community Access Grant Program - Urban Creek Access and Research for Recent Immigrant Youth Grant in the amount of $271,734.72 to develop programming to provide access to local natural resources, enhance science instruction, promote youth leadership development in service of sustaining natural resources, and support the wellbeing of recent immigrant students (known as "newcomers") in central East Oakland schools, via the English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement (ELLMA) Department, for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2024.
funding_source: California Department of Natural Resources, Youth Community Access Grant
headline: Applies for a $271,734.72 state grant for newcomer student nature programs in East Oakland
summary: The board approves the district applying to the California Department of Natural Resources for a grant to build programs that give recent immigrant students (known as "newcomers") access to local natural resources, strengthen science instruction and build youth leadership in central East Oakland schools. The grant period would run July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2024. This is an application, so the text does not say the money has been awarded.

title: First 5 (Five) of Alameda County - Contract for Services - Kindergarten Readiness - Neighborhoods Ready for School - Summer Learning Programs - Community Schools and Student Services Department

The money supports Summer Pre-K programs, training for early childhood and K-12 teachers, a School Readiness Coordinator, and financial relief for families with children ages 0-5 in the highest-need Oakland neighborhoods. It covers July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

summary: The board is adopting a resolution that makes the findings needed to hold meetings of district bodies covered by the Brown Act (California's open meetings law) virtually, in specified circumstances. The item has no cost.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Be the Change Consulting - Office of the Chief of Staff
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Be the Change Consulting, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide agenda creation, facilitation of design and planning sessions, and provide overall "backbone" support for all CORE Team, Black Student and Families Thriving Task Force, and Workgroup meetings; coordinate the activities of cross-functional teams, ensuring coherence across systems integration and direct alignment with the Resolution [Reparations for Black Students], via Office of the Chief of Staff, for the period of September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $91,250.00.
headline: Approves up to $91,250 for Be the Change Consulting to support Black student reparations task force work
summary: The board is approving a contract with Be the Change Consulting to create agendas, facilitate planning sessions and provide overall support for the CORE Team, the Black Student and Families Thriving Task Force and related workgroups. The work is tied to the board's Reparations for Black Students resolution. It runs September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022 and is capped at $91,250. The service period began before the board's vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Spearitwurx - Office of the Chief of Staff
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Spearitwurx, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide design and implementation of a healing-centered engagement strategy that informs the process and outcomes of the CORE Team and the Black Student and Families Thriving Task Force and also design, facilitate and document a series of community listening and learning sessions meant to inform the development of Black Thriving Indicators and recommendations aligned with the Reparations for Black Students Resolution, via Office of the Chief of Staff, for the period of September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $94,999.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $94,999 for Spearitwurx to run community listening sessions for Black Thriving Indicators
summary: The board is confirming a contract with Spearitwurx to design a healing-centered engagement approach for the CORE Team and the Black Student and Families Thriving Task Force. It will also run community listening sessions to help develop Black Thriving Indicators, tied to the Reparations for Black Students resolution. It runs September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022 and is capped at $94,999. The service period began before the board's vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Kirstin Hernandez - Office of the Chief of Staff
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Kirstin Hernandez, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide project management over the continued adoption and implementation of Parent Square, including the support of school sites and central office units, assistance with Help Desk Tickets, and collaboration with the IT team, via Office of the Chief of Staff, for the period of September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $95,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $95,000 for a project manager to run the ParentSquare communication rollout
summary: The board is confirming a contract with an individual contractor to manage the district's continued adoption of ParentSquare, a parent communication tool. The work includes supporting school sites and central offices, helping with help desk tickets and working with the IT team. It runs September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022 and is capped at $95,000. The service period began before the board's vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Across Lines, LLC - Student Assignment Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Across Lines, LLC, Ellensburg, WA, for the latter to analyze and present several options for a regional model of enrollment, using census block group data as well as attendance area data to provide multiple options of how the District could be divided into regions for elementary school enrollment: present  options as maps as well as through data tables, via Student Assignment Department, for the period of August 1, 2021 through May 1, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $7,500.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $7,500 for Across Lines to map options for regional elementary school enrollment
summary: The board is confirming a contract with Across Lines, LLC to analyze and present options for dividing the district into regions for elementary school enrollment. It will use census block group and attendance area data and present the options as maps and data tables for the Student Assignment Department. It runs August 1, 2021 through May 1, 2022 and is capped at $7,500. The service period began before the board's vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Reed Levitt - Student Assignment Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Reed Levitt, Berkeley, CA, for the latter to provide build out of a knowledge management tool in ZenDesk that will be available for families through the enrollment website and also will have a “staff only” section for Student Welcome Center staff; help develop an organizational structure, work with relevant offices to gather content (e.g., Office of Enrollment, Office of English Language Learners, Office of Early Childhood, and so forth), add the content into ZenDesk, launch the site, and train staff on how to use it; and also may support with project management across a few other enrollment projects, via Student Assignment Department, for the period of September 13, 2021 through January 15, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $4,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $4,000 for a contractor to build an enrollment help site for families in ZenDesk
summary: The board is confirming a contract with an individual contractor to build a ZenDesk knowledge website for families on the enrollment website, with a staff-only section for Student Welcome Center staff. The work includes gathering content from district offices, launching the site and training staff, and may include some project management. It runs September 13, 2021 through January 15, 2022 and is capped at $4,000. The service period began before the board's vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and William L. Winston, Education Consulting LLC, Oakland, CA, for the latter to ensure that partnership with colleges and universities for new teacher recruitment and pipelines are developed and maintained through development of Memorandums of Understanding, including Initiating contact with the designated staff at the college responsible for the MOU, communicating with the college and university partners about the MOU process, the writing of the MOU, and the negotiation of the MOU content, receiving approval from the District’s Legal Department, submitting and tracking the MOU through the approval process, via Talent / Human Resources Department, for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $10,000 for William L. Winston Education Consulting to set up college teacher-hiring partnerships

title: Amendment, No. 1, Services Agreement - COVID-19 Support – Oakland Public Education Fund – Office of the Chief of Staff
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and The Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide additional contact tracers to ensure that all cases are traced within a 24-hour period, including support in the training and implementation of the District’s testing program and contacting families to interview and advise them about next steps in response to an exposure, and test distribution drivers to ensure that the correct variety and quantity of tests get delivered to the appropriate school sites for the period July 1, 2021, through June 30, 2022, in the additional amount of $100,000.00, increasing the Agreement not to exceed amount from $250,000.00 to $350,000.00. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Adds $100,000 for Oakland Public Education Fund's COVID contact tracers and test delivery drivers
summary: This amendment adds $100,000 to an agreement with The Oakland Public Education Fund, raising the limit from $250,000 to $350,000. The added money pays for more contact tracers, who call families after an exposure and help train staff on the testing program, and for drivers who deliver tests to schools. The agreement covers July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.

title: First Addendum, Charter School Facilities Program Use Agreement - Education for Change Public Schools - Lazear Charter Academy - Office of Charter Schools
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of the First Addendum to Charter School Facilities Program Use Agreement For Education for Change Public Schools - Lazear Charter Academy, by and between the District and Education for Change Public Schools - Lazear Charter Academy, pursuant to terms and conditions stated therein including:

Starting in the 2021-22 fiscal year and continuing through the 2054-55 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay the following facilities use fee on a yearly basis: 

	(a) Starting in the 2021-2022 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 0.5% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined in Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

	(b) Starting in the 2030-31 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 0.75% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined in Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

	(c) Starting in the 2040-41 fiscal year, the Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 1% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined in Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

	(d) Starting in the 2050-51 fiscal year, the Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 2% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined in Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

However, for any school year in which the percentage of out-of-district students enrolled at Charter School is greater than ten percent (10%) on “Census Day” of that school year, the yearly facilities use fee shall be calculated as follows: 1) Fees shall be calculated pursuant to (a) through (d), above, for the percentage of enrollment that comprise in-District students, and 2) Fees shall be calculated pursuant to (e) through (h), below, for the percentage of enrollment that comprise out of District students. 

	(e) Starting in the 2021-2022 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 0.95% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined in Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

	(f) Starting in the 2030-2031 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 1.2% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined by Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

	(g) Starting in the 2040-2041 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 1.45% of the yearly revenue of the Charter school, as defined by Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f).

	(h) Starting in the 2050-2051 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 2.45% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined by Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 
	
All other terms of the Use Agreement remain unchanged and in full force and effect and apply to the terms set forth in the First Addendum.
headline: Sets long-term facilities fees for Lazear Charter Academy, rising from 0.5% to 2% of its revenue by 2050
summary: Education for Change Public Schools - Lazear Charter Academy will pay the district a yearly facilities use fee from 2021-22 through 2054-55. The fee is a share of the charter school's yearly revenue: 0.5%, rising in steps to 2%. If more than 10% of its students live outside the district, higher rates (0.95% rising to 2.45%) apply to those students. No dollar amount is stated.

Destination College Advising Corps (DCAC) to train, mentor and assign a fulltime, dedicated College Adviser Fellow to provide mentorship, promote college and career going culture through guidance and supervision of a Regional Manager at Oakland High School, for the period of August 2, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $18,000.00.
headline: Ratifies $18,000 for UC Berkeley's college adviser fellow at Oakland High School
summary: The Regents of the University of California's Center for Educational Partnerships will train, mentor and assign a full-time College Adviser Fellow through its Destination College Advising Corps to Oakland High School. The fellow promotes a college- and career-going culture, with supervision from a regional manager. The agreement runs August 2, 2021 to June 30, 2022, and the board is ratifying it after it began.
vendor_name: The Regents of the University of California, Center for Educational Partnerships
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Groundwork Education - Linked Learning Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Groundwork Education, Berkeley, CA, for the latter to provide Emergency Medical Services workshops and opportunities for certification for 30 students newcomer students, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, at Rudsdale Newcomer School, via Linked Learning Department, for the period of April 11, 2022 through May 25, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $15,540.00.
headline: Ratifies $15,540 for Groundwork Education emergency medical workshops for newcomer students
summary: Groundwork Education will provide emergency medical services workshops and certification opportunities for 30 newcomer students at Rudsdale Newcomer School. The agreement runs April 11 to May 25, 2022, and the board is ratifying it after it began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Oakland Youth Chorus - Claremont Middle School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Oakland Youth Chorus, Oakland, CA, for the latter to support the school in designing, creating, implementing and evaluating a school based music program whether through virtual, in person or a hybrid program delivery model, as set forth in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, at Claremont Middle School, for the period of August 28, 2021 through May 26, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $20,000.00.
headline: Ratifies $20,000 for Oakland Youth Chorus to help build a music program at Claremont Middle School
summary: Oakland Youth Chorus will help Claremont Middle School design, create, carry out and evaluate a school-based music program, delivered virtually, in person or in a hybrid model. The agreement runs August 28, 2021 to May 26, 2022, and the board is ratifying it after it began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc - OPSR Counseling Department
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc, Oakland, CA, for the latter, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement,  to partner with District’s Central Academic Recovery team’s summer learning experience for 9th & 10th graders to empower, inspire self-awareness through art, creativity and education, with participants  learning to make positive choices to break the cycle of violence for themselves and their
communities, choose peace over conflict and love over fear, via OPSR Counseling Department, for the period of June 2, 2022 through July 8, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00.
headline: Ratifies $5,000 for Attitudinal Healing Connection's summer violence-prevention arts program
summary: Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc. will partner with the district's Central Academic Recovery summer learning program for 9th and 10th graders. It uses art, creativity and education to build self-awareness and help students make positive choices and choose peace over conflict. The agreement runs June 2 to July 8, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Mills College - LIFE Academy
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Mills College, Oakland, CA, for the latter to support the school’s Multi-Tiered Systems of Support team by creating and facilitating a customized workshop for the team in early June that will support school to use what has been learned about supporting students with academic, attendance and behavioral needs and to plan for next school year with goals and students at the center, stated in Exhibit A of Agreement,  for LIFE Academy, for the period of May 30, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $4,000.00.
headline: Pays Mills College up to $4,000 for a student-support team workshop at LIFE Academy
summary: Mills College will create and lead a customized workshop in early June for LIFE Academy's team that supports students with academic, attendance and behavior needs. The team will use it to apply what it has learned and plan for next school year. The agreement runs May 30 to June 30, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Rigorous Love - LIFE Academy
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Rigorous Love, Oakland, CA, for the latter to support parent group, Parent Academy, with two professional learning sessions to be held in both Spanish and English, with the first being on anti-Black racism within the Raza community and the second being on Restorative Justice and the circle process and school’s approach to discipline through a restorative lens, as stated in Exhibit A of Agreement, at  Life Academy, for the period of May 2, 2022 through May 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $2,060.00.
headline: Ratifies $2,060 for Rigorous Love to lead two parent workshops at LIFE Academy
summary: Rigorous Love will lead two professional learning sessions, in Spanish and English, for LIFE Academy's Parent Academy group. One covers anti-Black racism within the Raza community, and the other covers restorative justice and the school's approach to discipline. The agreement runs May 2 to May 30, 2022, and the board is ratifying it after it began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Hillary Walker - LIFE Academy
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Hillary Walker, Oakland, CA, for the latter to plan and co-lead a group of students on a public health pathway "post session" through which 20 pathways students will be exposed to a variety of public health experiences linked to their pathway projects, including a week long out of state public health field trip connected to the post session and projects, as stated in Exhibit A of Agreement at Life Academy, for the period of April 1, 2022 through May 26, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $8,000.00.
headline: Ratifies $8,000 for a consultant to lead a public health field trip for LIFE Academy students
summary: An Oakland consultant will plan and co-lead a public health pathway "post session" for 20 LIFE Academy students. It includes public health experiences linked to their projects and a week-long out-of-state field trip. The agreement runs April 1 to May 26, 2022, and the board is ratifying it after it began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Earth Team - Skyline High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Earth Team, Richmond, CA, for the latter to provide opportunities for students to engage in real world work experiences through their Sustainable Youth Program, a long term approach to environmental education by working with individual core schools to offer a variety of projects-from short-term class visits to yearlong after school internships-all with a multi-year approach that caters to the unique needs of students and their respective schools with this year’s  projects focusing on waste, watersheds, litter and a brand new urban forestry project, stated in Exhibit A of Agreement,  at Skyline High School, for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $5,600.00.
headline: Ratifies $5,600 for Earth Team's environmental work experiences at Skyline High School
summary: Earth Team of Richmond will give Skyline High School students real-world work experiences through its Sustainable Youth Program, from class visits to year-long after-school internships. This year's projects focus on waste, watersheds, litter and a new urban forestry project. The agreement runs July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022, and the board is ratifying it after it began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Global Seed - Oakland High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Global Seed, Oakland, CA, for the latter to manage and coordinate Y-PLAN Oakland action research projects and partnerships between teachers and civic clients by fostering development of key partners and stakeholders within District, the city, and the region, and developing civic work-based learning projects for 2021-22, with this Agreement, as delineated in Exhibit A, to improve student engagement in  Pathways  by empowering students through community-based action research projects that create more relevant and dynamic learning opportunities for Oakland High School, for the period of August 9, 2021 through May 31, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00.
headline: Ratifies $10,000 for Global Seed to run Y-PLAN community research projects at Oakland High School
summary: Global Seed will manage and coordinate Y-PLAN Oakland action research projects and partnerships between teachers and civic clients, including city and regional partners. The aim is to improve student engagement in pathways through community-based projects at Oakland High School. The agreement runs August 9, 2021 to May 31, 2022, and the board is ratifying it after it began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Niroga Institute - OPSR Counseling Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Niroga Institute, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide a trained instructor to collaborate alongside a credentialed Biology teacher to implement its vision of creating a mindful generation for a more connected and compassionate world as an extension of the NGSS aligned Biology unit about the Stress Response;  promote equity by teaching students and adults trauma-informed dynamic mindfulness, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, via OPSR Counseling Department, for the period of June 2, 2022, through July 8, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $4,500.00.
headline: Ratifies $4,500 for Niroga Institute's mindfulness instruction in summer biology classes
summary: Niroga Institute will provide a trained instructor to work with a credentialed biology teacher, teaching students and adults trauma-informed dynamic mindfulness as an extension of a biology unit on the stress response. The work is part of the district's summer learning program and is arranged through the counseling department. The agreement runs June 2 to July 8, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Oakland Public Education Fund - Skyline High School
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide students with mental health support including regular one-on-one meetings and group sessions for students; coordinate with Coordination of Services Team (COST), Leadership Team, and Culture Team to identify high risk students and initiate connection as well as work as part of emergency mental health response team at Skyline High School, for the period of October 1, 2021, through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $44,560.00.
headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $44,560 for student mental health support at Skyline High
summary: The Oakland Public Education Fund will provide Skyline High School students with mental health support, including one-on-one meetings and group sessions. It will work with school teams to identify high-risk students and be part of the emergency mental health response team. The agreement runs October 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022, and the board is approving it after that start date.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Vincent Yu - Franklin Elementary School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement  2021-2022 by and between the District and Vincent Yu, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide additional hours as a community liaison assisting with minor conflict resolution, conducting small group intervention for positive student interactions during the school day, for the period of October 07, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in the additional amount of $5,000.00, increasing the Agreement not to exceed amount from $15,000.00 to $20,000.00.  All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Ratifies $5,000 more, to $20,000 total, for a community liaison at Franklin Elementary School
summary: This amendment adds hours for a community liaison at Franklin Elementary School who helps with minor conflict resolution and runs small-group activities for positive student interactions. It adds $5,000, raising the contract limit from $15,000 to $20,000, and the board is ratifying it after the fact. All other terms stay the same.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Our Family Coalition - Network 4
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Our Family Coalition, San Francisco, CA, for the latter to provide a professional training series for all Network 4 principals on a weekly basis for 2 hours, covering topics that include inclusive school trainings that will create more welcoming schools and agencies to serve LGBTQ families and their allies. Additionally, principals will implement more equitable practices to serve lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer families and their allies, via Network 4, for the period of April 1, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00.
headline: Ratifies $5,000 for Our Family Coalition to train Network 4 principals on welcoming LGBTQ families
summary: Our Family Coalition of San Francisco will lead a weekly two-hour training series for all Network 4 principals on inclusive schools and more equitable practices for serving LGBTQ families and their allies. The agreement runs April 1 to June 30, 2022, and the board is ratifying it after it began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - College Summit dba PeerForward - Fremont High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and College Summit, Inc dba PeerForward, Washington, DC, for the latter to conduct a two (2) hour virtual orientation and Leadership Development session and conduct a Training Workshop that focuses on the ins and outs of the college admissions process, master leadership skills, and community organizing techniques; and post-training, assist participants to execute three powerful campaigns to get their peers to college, as stated in Exhibit A of the Agreement, at Fremont High School, for the period of March 1, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $12,000.00.
headline: Ratifies $12,000 for PeerForward college-going leadership training at Fremont High School
summary: College Summit, Inc., doing business as PeerForward, will run a virtual orientation and leadership session and a training workshop on college admissions, leadership and community organizing for Fremont High School students. After training, it will help participants run three campaigns to get peers to college. The agreement runs March 1 to June 30, 2022, and the board is ratifying it after it began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Community Development Finance - Linked Learning Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Community Development Finance, Oakland, CA, for the latter, as directed by District’s Central Academic Recovery lead, to distribute stipends to students participating in select credit recovery programs as part of District’s set of strategies to address COVID learning loss, via Linked Learning Department, for the period of May 16, 2022, through August 8, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $18,000.00.
headline: Ratifies $18,000 for Community Development Finance to distribute credit-recovery stipends to students
summary: Community Development Finance will distribute stipends to students in select credit recovery programs, as directed by the district's Central Academic Recovery lead. The programs are part of the district's strategy to address learning loss from COVID. The agreement runs May 16 to August 8, 2022, and the board is ratifying it.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Student Travel - Chicago, Illinois - National Restorative Justice Conference - Edna Brewer Middle School
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0199 - Authorization for Approval of Student Travel - by school site Edna Brewer Middle School, for 20 students and 6 adults, as specified in Out of State Field Trip/Excursion Request, attached, to attend the National Community Restorative Justice Conference in Chicago, Illinois, as described in the itinerary, for the period of July 6, 2022 through July 9, 2022, at no cost to the District.

summary: The Board approves travel to Chicago, Illinois for 20 Edna Brewer Middle School students and 6 adults to attend the National Community Restorative Justice Conference. The trip runs July 6 through July 9, 2022. It comes at no cost to the District.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Oakland Public Education Fund - Student Assignment Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide through Youth Beat at KDOL, a fiscal project of the Fund, the production of 11 videos incorporating school personnel and voices that detail the primary offerings of each site, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via Student Assignment Department, for the period of February 1, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $25,000.00.

summary: The District hires the Oakland Public Education Fund, working through its Youth Beat at KDOL project, to produce 11 videos that use school staff and voices to describe what each school offers. The work is done for the Student Assignment Department from February 1 through June 30, 2022. The cost cannot exceed $25,000.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Oakland School of the Arts - J-13A Waiver - Loss of Attendance and Instructional Time - COVID-19 Pandemic
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0083 - Approval of Oakland School of the Arts (OSA) J-13A Waiver.

summary: The Board adopts a resolution approving a J-13A waiver request for Oakland School of the Arts. According to the title, the waiver concerns attendance and instructional time lost during the COVID-19 pandemic. The text states no dollar amount.

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - FM3 Research - Office of General Counsel
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and FM3 Research, Oakland, CA, for the latter to conduct survey research among District voters on issues related to a potential parcel tax measure, as specified in Exhibit A, (FM3 Proposal December 8, 2021), via Office of the General Counsel, for the period of January 1, 2022 through May 31, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $36,500.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $36,500 for FM3 Research to survey voters on a possible parcel tax
summary: The District hired FM3 Research to conduct survey research among District voters on issues related to a potential parcel tax measure. The contract covers January 1 through May 31, 2022, so the Board is approving it after the work period began. The cost cannot exceed $36,500, paid from the General Purpose fund.

title: Change Order No. 1, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – N. V. Heathorn Company – The Center Foster School Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Agreement Between Owner and Contractor of Change Order No. 1 by and between the District and N.V. Heathorn Company, Concord, CA, for the latter to provide additional construction services, which consist of repairing a cart wash duct & ceiling, repairing a leaking steam valve and pipes, replace and remove duroblocks, remove old VFDs from the roof, and fix a broken heat recovery pipe connected to refrigeration equipment, for The Center at Foster Project, in the amount of $16,980.00, increasing the contract price from $16,346.00 to $33,326.00 and extending the term of Agreement from September 23, 2021 through December 31, 2021, by 181 days, to June 30, 2022.

official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution 2122-0228 - Award of Bid … in Response to RFP#21-108SWC, and Services Agreement 2021-2022 to Blenderbox, Inc., New York, NY, in an amount not to exceed Five Hundred Seventy Thousand Dollars ($570,000.00), as the responsive, responsible bidder, for District’s Student Application System (License), via Technology Services Department, for the period May 26, 2022 through June 30, 2025.

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Claudine Gossett Photography - Chief Systems and Services Officer
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Claudine Gossett Photography, Berkeley, CA, for the latter, bringing professional equipment needed to each site, and under the guidance of the Nutrition Services Project Manager, take photos at seven schools during breakfast and lunch periods and provide Nutrition Services with digital images from which to select photos for printing, via the Office of the Chief of Systems and Services, for the period of April 11, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00.

flags: pulled_from_consent; raises_existing_contract; large_increase; source_issue; previously_delayed; multi_year
source_issue: The text describes the $1,000,000 as raising the agreement's 'year 1' amount from $306,609.00 to $1,306,609.00, but the attached agreement and amendment show these are the not-to-exceed amounts for the whole October 2020 to September 2023 term.

title: Blanket Student Accident Insurance - Premium Payment - Fiscal Year 2022-2023 - Risk Management Department
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education, as Policyholder, of Application To ACE American and Participant Agreement, and authorization of payment, Fiscal Year 2022-2023, for Blanket Student Accident Insurance, Policy No. SDA N104206563 underwritten by ACE American Insurance Company, to Myers-Stevens & Toohey & Company, Inc., Mission Viejo, CA, (Broker) as follows for:

SCOPE OF COVERAGE:

School-Time Coverage - Covers all enrolled students for Injuries sustained while on campus during the hours and on the days school is in session; for up to 1 hour before school starts and 1 hour after school ends while on campus; while participating in school sponsored and supervised activities, including all interscholastic sports and summer activities; and traveling directly to and from: home and school to attend regularly scheduled classes; traveling to and from school and off campus locations to participate in school sponsored and supervised activities, provided such travel is arranged by and is under the direction of the School, or in School Vehicles, anytime. Also covers non-students for injury sustained while engaged in “student shadowing” for the purpose of evaluating possible enrollment. Covers students participating in school sponsored and approved Work Study programs and Community Service activities.

not to exceed a cumulative cost of $75,846.87.
headline: Pays up to $75,846.87 for 2022-23 blanket accident insurance covering all enrolled students
summary: The board approves the application and payment for the district's Blanket Student Accident Insurance for fiscal year 2022-2023. The policy is underwritten by ACE American Insurance Company, and payment goes to the broker, Myers-Stevens & Toohey & Company, Inc. It covers all enrolled students for injuries on campus, at school-sponsored activities and on direct trips to and from school, up to $75,846.87.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Catastrophic Accident Insurance for Students and Volunteers – Premium Payment - Fiscal Year 2021-2022 - Risk Management Department
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education, as Policyholder, of 2022-2023 School Year Coverage Request Form, and authorization of payment, Fiscal Year 2022-023, for Catastrophic Accident Insurance for Students and Volunteers, underwritten by ACE American Insurance Company, to Myers-Stevens & Toohey & Company, Inc., Mission Viejo, CA (Broker), as follows:

Class I - Interscholastic Athletics
Covers students while participating in school sponsored and directly supervised games and official practice sessions of interscholastic sports and supporting activities (band, cheerleaders, majorettes, student coaches, student trainers, and student managers) and while traveling directly and without interruption between school and the site of such activities, provided that such travel is arranged by and is at the direction of the school.
COST: 2536 participants x $4.12 = $10,448.32; and

Coverage II - Student Activities

Covers students while on premises when school is in session and while participating in school sponsored and directly supervised activities (except interscholastic athletics), and while traveling directly and without interruption between school and the site of such activities, provided that such travel is arranged by and is at the direction of the school, and while traveling directly and without interruption between home and school to attend regularly scheduled classes (includes one hour immediately before and after regularly scheduled classes).
COST: 34566 participants x $1.26 = $43,533.16,
not to exceed a cumulative cost of $54,001.48.
headline: Pays up to $54,001.48 for 2022-23 catastrophic accident insurance for students and volunteers
summary: The board approves the 2022-2023 coverage request and payment for catastrophic accident insurance for students and volunteers, underwritten by ACE American Insurance Company and paid through the broker Myers-Stevens & Toohey & Company, Inc. It has two parts: one for interscholastic athletics and one for other school activities. Total cost is capped at $54,001.48.
source_issue: The text prints the Coverage II cost as $43,533.16, but 34,566 participants x $1.26 is $43,553.16 (as shown in the attached form), so the two line items total the stated $54,001.48; the title also says Fiscal Year 2021-2022 while the text and attachment say 2022-2023.

title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2021-2022 and Amendment, No. 1, Data Sharing Agreement 2021-2022 – Grand River Solutions - Chief Governance Officer
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2021-2022 and Amendment No. 1, Data Sharing Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Grand River Solutions, Saratoga, CA, for the latter to provide additional services as a Decision-Making Authority for Title IX matters as assigned by the Legal Department and consists of managing logistics of the decision-making process, resolving procedural disputes that arise during the process, draft/finalize a written decision with analysis, rationale, factual findings, and all elements in accordance with District policies and procedures and Title IX, more specifically delineated in the Scope of Work (Amended), in an additional not to exceed amount of $135,000 over the term of the agreement, increasing Agreement’s not-to-exceed amount from $95,000 to $230,000, and extending the term of the Services and Data Sharing Agreement from December 1, 2021 through June 30, 2023 to June 30, 2024. All other terms and conditions of the Agreements remain in full force and effect.
headline: Adds $135,000 to Grand River Solutions' Title IX decision-maker contract, now up to $230,000
summary: Grand River Solutions acts as the decision-making authority for Title IX cases (federal rules on sex-based discrimination and harassment in schools) that the Legal Department assigns. This change adds $135,000, raising the contract limit from $95,000 to $230,000, and extends the end date from June 30, 2023 to June 30, 2024. It amends both the services agreement and a data sharing agreement. All other terms stay the same.
pulled_from_consent: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (6–0), instead of with the rest of the consent report.
outcome_action: Adopted

title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - The Segal Company - Risk Management Department
